title: Choose the visual world for StudySpots UB
question: The roll assigned High Blue Sky. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: High Blue Sky
options.lineage: Ulaanbaatar's 250 clear days a year: the deep high-altitude blue and its hard noon light
options.thesis: The app as a slice of UB's sky: one committed blue field whose tone follows the city's real time of day, so 'right now' is felt before it is read.
options.viewport: A sky band owns the top: name, search and filters set white on blue, its tone tracking UB's clock (noon blue, dusk orange edge, night navy); the map is the ground below and place cards are white sheets casting hard noon shadows.
options.risk: A big flat blue can read as a generic brand blue if the sky clock and the hard light are not fully committed.

raised.raise: Every figure (Mbps, metres, minutes ago, reports) set in tabular numerals as a compact data strip, never buried in prose.
One type family at a strict stepped scale; live busyness set large enough to read at arm's length outdoors.
Strict ply: page, card and dialog each get exactly one hard-shadow depth; nothing floats without one.

options.label: Bus Stop Board
options.thesis: Every place is a stop on a route board: its name, its number, and how soon you can get a seat.
options.viewport: A yellow route board heads the screen with the nearest places as numbered stops, busyness as arrival-style countdown blocks.
options.risk: The most familiar of the set: wayfinding yellow-on-black is close to what transit and map apps already ship.

options.label: Departures Board
options.lineage: boarding pass and live gate board
options.thesis: Places as rows on a live departures board, reranking in place as seats free up.
options.viewport: A board of nearby places ranked by 'seats free now', the selected place's pass beside it with hours and Wi-Fi as stub segments.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: busyness becomes a live rerank, which is the clearest 'where now'; loses on local identification.
options.risk: Can feel like an airport, not a city, if the board grammar is applied to everything.

options.label: Catalog Wall
options.thesis: Places as poster rows (Open now, Quiet now, Saved) where the focused tile expands to tell you what it is.
options.viewport: Horizontal rows of place photos by situation, the focused tile showing busyness, hours and Wi-Fi.
options.case: Fuses: rows map to real situations and browsing is clear; loses on identification because it reads as any streaming app.
options.risk: User photos vary wildly in quality, and the wall depends on them.

options.label: Graph Paper Grid
options.lineage: Wim Crouwel grid specimens, via every student's graph-paper notebook
options.thesis: The city on a visible construction grid: places snap to cells, numbers and names built from the same armature.
options.viewport: A gridded sheet with the map as one cell block and place cards snapping into the columns beside it.
options.case: Fuses through students' graph-paper notebooks; holds identification, weaker at answering 'where now'.
options.risk: The grid can turn into decoration and crowd small Cyrillic text.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: Places as barcode columns of pure black and white data.
options.viewport: A barcode field with one column per place, selection pulling its numbers into focus.
options.case: Loses both axes: strobing data reads as art, not as where to study.
options.risk: Unusable outdoors and for anyone not already fluent in it.
options.kept: Numbers as a disciplined tabular data strip.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.thesis: Place names in proud pixel letterforms at poster scale.
options.viewport: A giant pixel headline of the nearest place over dense columns.
options.case: Loses both axes: bitmap Cyrillic hurts reading and says nothing about places.
options.risk: Novelty that ages in a week.
options.kept: A strict stepped type scale, one family repeated at set sizes.

options.label: Acetate Manual
options.thesis: Each section a coloured divider board under clear acetate leaves.
options.viewport: A tab rail of categories down the edge, place content on hinged leaves.
options.case: Loses both axes: manual-reading is not how people pick a café on the street.
options.risk: Heavy layering slows a quick decision.
options.kept: Strict layer discipline: one shadow depth per layer.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean map-and-listings app: white cards, place photos, stars, one brand blue.
canonCard.viewport: Map beside a list of photo cards with ratings, filters as rounded chips.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Google Maps-style listings by design.
